findings.finding: Consensus Q3 underlying growth for Consulting is 4.7% with MMC at 7.1%, which implies Mercer at roughly 3.3%, while Mercer printed +5% underlying in both Q1 and Q2 2026, faces an easy Q3 2025 comp (+3%), and management said on the Q2 call it expects Mercer's growth momentum to continue and MMC to grow mid-to-high single digits; Accenture's FQ4 (to Aug-31) consulting revenue +6% corroborates demand.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (2025-10-16): consulting was the strong line (OW/MMC +8% underlying) and the stock fell 8.52% on flat RIS margins; Q1 2026 (2026-04-16) 'beat on Mercer unit strength' bought +4.39%. Consulting strength alone has not protected the stock when RIS disappoints.
findings.why_not_priced: The headline bar (EPS $1.96, revenue $6.63B, underlying 3.9%) is built on a consulting estimate below the segment's own H1 run-rate; if the market priced Mercer at its 5% run-rate, the Zacks consulting estimate would read ~5.5-6%, not 4.7%. It is a segment estimate from one aggregator, so this is partly a stale-estimate inference, not a disclosed number. Net of the rest: consulting is ~39% of revenue, so a 1pt consulting beat is ~0.4pt on consolidated underlying (~$25M revenue, ~$0.02-0.03 EPS); RIS (~61%) has to hold at ~3.5% for this to show as a clean beat. MMC's 7.1% sits inside the company's mid-to-high single-digit guide, so only the Mercer part is outside what was guided.
findings.independence: Company primary documents: Q1 2026 release (Mercer +5%, MMC +6%) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/62709/000006270926000096/mmc1q2026ex991newsrelease.htm ; Q2 2026 release (Consulting +8%, Mercer +5%, MMC +13%) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000062709/000006270926000193/mmc2q2026ex991newsrelease.htm ; Q3 2025 comp (Consulting +5%) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/62709/000006270925000123/mmc3q2025ex991newsrelease.htm . Different-source corroboration of consulting demand: Accenture FQ4 FY26 consulting revenue +6% USD, 2026-10-01, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001467373/000146737326000037/q4fy26earnings8-kexhibit.htm (a proxy; Accenture is IT-heavy).

findings.finding: Consensus has Guy Carpenter Q3 revenue up 0.5% against a +5% Q3 2025 comp, after Guy Carpenter printed -2% underlying in Q2 2026 and its own global property-cat rate-on-line index fell 16% at the July 1 renewals, an acceleration from -12% at January 1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-21): Guy Carpenter -2% underlying was the headline negative in trade coverage and the stock closed -0.28%, then rallied ~12% over the next six sessions; Q3 2025 had GC +5% and the stock still fell 8.52%. GC has not been the line that moves this stock.
findings.source_date: 2026-07 (July 1 2026 renewals report; URL path on guycarp.com is /insights/2026/07/)
findings.why_not_priced: If the reinsurance softening were fully reflected, the GC estimate would sit near or below Q2's -2% rather than at +0.5% against a tough comp. Net of the rest: Guy Carpenter is only ~$400M of ~$6.6B Q3 revenue (~6%), so a 3pt miss on GC is ~$12M, ~0.2pt of consolidated revenue and ~0.3pt of RIS underlying; Marsh Risk (~$3.6B, running +4%) dominates RIS and is the line that would have to soften for this to matter. The reinsurance softening itself is public and widely covered, which is why this is small.
findings.independence: Company primary document: Q2 2026 release, Guy Carpenter -2% underlying, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000062709/000006270926000193/mmc2q2026ex991newsrelease.htm ; Q3 2025 comp GC +5%, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/62709/000006270925000123/mmc3q2025ex991newsrelease.htm . Different source on the same renewal data: JP Morgan via Insurance Business, 'no near-term floor as reinsurance rates fall 16% at midyear', https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/reinsurance/news/breaking-news/jp-morgan-sees-no-nearterm-floor-as-reinsurance-rates-fall-16-at-midyear-581535.aspx (same underlying index, so not independent of the fact).

findings.finding: Gallagher, speaking on 2026-09-23 after two months of the quarter (after Marsh last spoke on 2026-07-21), held Q3 brokerage organic at ~5% with 'further confidence' in ~6% company-wide, and reported US retail property renewal premium changes easing to about -7% in July-August from about -12% in Q2, with ex-property renewals up ~3-4%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Marsh Risk organic is the line this stock trades on: Q3 2025 RIS +3% with flat margins -> -8.52%; Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 with Marsh Risk ~4% -> +5.47% and +4.39%; Q2 2026 Marsh Risk +4%, RIS +3% -> -0.28%.
findings.why_not_priced: Gallagher's update was public, but the broker group sold off through September regardless (AJG 262.69 on 09-04 to 229.64 on 09-23, MRSH 185.74 to 170.38) and the skew on MRSH still pays for downside; if the market had read the counterparty's 'property declines easing, brokerage organic intact' as applying to Marsh, the put skew would be flatter and the RIS estimate would not be at 3.5%. It is a proxy: Gallagher is middle-market-weighted while Marsh is large-account and property-cat heavy, and WTW's CLIPS reported large-account pricing turning negative for the first time since 2017, which cuts against the read-through for Marsh specifically - hence the small size.
findings.independence: Counter-evidence from a different source: CIAB Q2 2026 survey, large accounts -3.7%, property -6.3%, 2026-08-20, https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/national/2026/08/20/882240.htm ; WTW large accounts first price drop since 2017, https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/us/news/breaking-news/large-commercial-accounts-see-first-price-drop-since-2017-wtw-finds-589348.aspx ; Marsh's own Q2 2026 index -6% global (property -12%), https://www.marsh.com/en/corp/about/news/global-commercial-insurance-falls-6-percent-q2-2026.html . These are Q2 data; Gallagher's is the only Jul-Aug datapoint found.

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly positive while the skew (+3.4, downside paid) and last year's -8.5% Q3 reaction lean negative and the 5-day run-up (+2.6%) has already taken back part of the September drawdown; with no company-level number the market has not seen, I side with neither strongly and keep p_up at 52.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 and rule 9 (reaction function; segment net of the rest): consulting finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3, because this stock trades on RIS (Q3 2025 had strong consulting and fell 8.5%) and only the Mercer part sits outside what the company guided.
Rule 9: Guy Carpenter finding cut from -0.3 to -0.2, since GC is ~6% of Q3 revenue and Marsh Risk dominates RIS.
Rule 5 (proxy; macro-to-company transmission): Gallagher read-through cut from +0.3 to +0.2, because Gallagher is middle-market-weighted and the large-account series (WTW, CIAB) points the other way.
Rule 7 (sign against a positive skew): p_up moved from 53 to 52; abs_move_pct left at 4.0.
Left standing: fiduciary income at 0 (inside guide); bar sourced to two agreeing estimate sources plus a company guide, so no cap needed; short interest checked, not crowded.
